correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=1, exact right-value Hermite cardinal R_m(z)=z^m sum_{k=0}^{m-1} binom(m+k-1,k)(1-z)^k has top coefficient (-1)^(m-1)binom(2m-2,m-1). Scaled local polynomial expansions yield a uniform L2 collision limit in which the bounded derivative noises vanish. The smooth Hermite remainder is uniformly bounded. A deterministic global |X-Y|^d E upper bound makes the rescaled two-dimensional density integral compact; bounded convergence supplies the positive exact tail constant. The layer-cake formula gives all p moment endpoints. The standalone exact-rational checker verifies 281 counted constraints/scalings for finite m but is not substituted for the proof.

evidence: Batenkov–Diab (arxiv:2203.11923, Sections 1–3) proves deterministic worst-case singular-value/minimax scaling of *Fourier* confluent Vandermonde matrices for clustered Dirac models, but does not integrate iid *real* node collisions or produce the exact global L2 noise-error tail constant. Niu–Zhang–Zhou (arxiv:2207.01852, intro and method) treats numerical Arnoldi bases rather than the error distribution of the square Hermite interpolant.

Zhang et al. (arxiv:2404.09266, introduction and Section 4 applications) considers G-Arnoldi and multivariate overdetermined Hermite least squares; its stable basis and node sampling are different from exact two-node interpolation. Gautschi (DOI 10.1007/BF01432880, abstract only) provides deterministic inverse-norm bounds that might imply a coarser collision rate but cannot be represented as checked for the random-tail coefficient.

Their worst-case bounds do not give the random iid-node global-error tail coefficient; the result is not a mere corollary of a stated probability theorem.

The claim is limited to that exact constant plus its moment cutoff, and does not claim that classical cardinal polynomials or conditioning asymptotics themselves are new.

The closest retrieved published interpolation findings concern monotone range overshoot for deterministic three/four-knot natural-cubic, Lagrange, or Floater–Hormann schemes, with no iid-noise node-collision distribution. A related Lagrange comparison has value-only one-per-cell *stratified* node sampling and a different collision-density exponent; neither its domain nor its statement dominates the present two-node confluent noisy-jet law.

originality.rationale: Distinctive all-order unconditional iid-knot Pareto tail coefficient and exact moment cutoff have not been implied by the inspected source statements. Deterministic conditioning, stable-basis interpolation and fixed-grid overshoot are insufficient to establish the distributional constant. Priority remains qualified because unindexed historical probabilistic interpolation could contain an equivalent result.

Search-ranking databases cannot establish universal novelty; independent publication-priority assessment is still needed.

value.rationale: Noisy Hermite derivative interpolation at independently sampled nodes is a natural exact reconstruction model. The new sharp all-order Pareto coefficient and moment threshold quantify a strong risk undetected by finite typical-error plots: even bounded measurement noise creates infinite mean global L2 error; higher derivative multiplicity worsens the power to 1/(2m-1). The coefficient distinguishes value-noise from derivative-noise contribution. It is not a mere relabeling or an unmotivated finite slice; limitations and operationally relevant alternatives (minimum separation, regularization) are explicit.
